title: Comparing Freshdesk Pricing 2026 Plans and Costs
summary: Freshdesk pricing tiers vary based on specific feature requirements and agent counts. Use this breakdown to calculate your actual monthly expenses.
body_markdown:
## Freshdesk pricing plans and core feature limits


Functionality is segmented by team size and operational complexity at[Freshdesk](https://www.freshdesk.com/pricing) . The pricing structure uses feature gating to separate basic ticket management from advanced AI-driven automation.


While the entry-level tiers provide the infrastructure for customer communication, moving from a reactive to a proactive support model requires jumping tiers to unlock SLA management and multi-channel routing.


The following table illustrates how Freshdesk distributes its core capabilities across the four primary service levels:


Tier Cost (Annual/Monthly) Agent Limit Core Features


Free $0 2 Agents Basic ticketing, Knowledge base, Social media integration


Growth Paid Per Agent Unlimited Automation rules, Collision detection, Custom SSL


Pro Paid Per Agent Unlimited SLA management, Multilingual support, Custom roles


Enterprise Paid Per Agent Unlimited Skill-based routing, Sandbox, Audit logs, AI bots


*Prices and plan limits checked against[support.freshdesk.com](https://support.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/50000010099-explore-freshdesk-free-program-freshdesk-only-) on October 10, 2026.*


As a team’s internal governance requirements grow (such as the need for distinct permissions or environment testing) this progression ensures the per-user cost scales accordingly.


### The Free plan for small teams


Startups may find a foundational helpdesk in the Free plan, but a **two-agent limit** caps its utility and prevents it from supporting growing departments.


According to[Freshdesk](https://support.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/50000010099-explore-freshdesk-free-program-freshdesk-only-) , this program is available for free for 6 months for new businesses, giving startups a significant runway to scale before incurring software expenses, which means early-stage companies can preserve their limited capital during their most critical growth phase.


Once the introductory period expires, teams must prepare for a budget transition. Because it lacks automation and custom ticket views, agents must manually categorize every interaction, which creates a labor bottleneck as soon as ticket volume exceeds what two people can handle.


### Growth: The entry-level paid tier


By removing the agent cap and introducing basic automation, the Growth tier allows teams to trigger actions based on ticket events like status changes.


It introduces "Collision Detection," which alerts agents when another person is viewing the same ticket so they do not send duplicate responses to a customer.


When developers need to extend these workflows to external tools, they often use[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) to bridge the gap between Freshdesk events and third-party databases without manual data entry.


Activepieces charges 1 credit per flow run regardless of how many steps or integrations are involved, which allows teams to build granular, multi-stage logic without the per-task tax found on other platforms.


This predictable metering, visible on the published pricing page, ensures that a ten-step data validation process costs the same as a simple two-step notification.


### Freshdesk Pro tier features and SLA management


Service Level Agreement (SLA) management is introduced at the Pro tier. This is the only way for managers to set automated deadlines for ticket resolution based on business hours.


It also unlocks "Custom Roles," so an administrator can give a contractor access to respond to tickets without giving them the power to delete the entire customer database.


For companies operating in multiple regions, the Pro tier is the lowest level providing "Multilingual Knowledge Base" support. This forces a migration for any team that needs to serve customers in more than one language.


### Enterprise: High-volume support requirements


Organizations that require strict change management and automated resource allocation are the target for the Enterprise tier. It is the only tier that includes a "Sandbox" environment.


Developers can test new workflows against a copy of their setup without risking a configuration error that breaks the live customer portal.


It also features "Skill-based Routing," which automatically assigns tickets to agents based on their specific expertise rather than just their current availability. This prevents complex technical queries from landing in the queue of a generalist.
